response.summary: The plan is well structured. Credential-free gates, the owner gate on the upstream PR text, and the pinning are handled well. Two problems are blocking. First, the mapping marks reference/sample populations as 'out of scope', which is not one of the four dispositions predicate 3 requires, so a real metaschema element is silently lost. Second, predicate 4's differential check has no independent evaluator for 'the formula's meaning'. The hardening concerns are: the identity digest under the sidecar fallback, consumer-limitation rows in a runtime loss report, an ungated public fork push, the import digest order, an unpinned fork converter in OS6-C2, and 'native + extension' rows that conflict with 'exactly one disposition'. A few consistency gaps remain around OS6 and close, and the OD numbering in the status line.

evidence.observation: The mapping marks '`reference_populations`, sample populations | none in the ontology; mappings are layer 1 | out of scope'. `reference_populations` is a top-level field in the GND model schema, while predicate 3 promises a disposition for every model element and predicate 5 promises an equal round trip.

concerns.recommendation: Give these fields an explicit extension or refusal disposition and specify how round-trip equality handles them.
concerns.title: Model populations fall outside the disposition and round-trip contracts

evidence.observation: The CLI makes the report optional in '`gnd export ossie MODEL --out FILE [--loss-report FILE]`', while OD6 says 'Exit 0 with the loss report' when constructs are refused. No default report destination is specified.

concerns.recommendation: Specify a guaranteed report destination or require an explicit report path whenever export succeeds with a refused disposition; fail if the report cannot be written.
concerns.title: A successful lossy export may have no visible loss report

evidence.observation: Predicate 3 requires 'Every model element has exactly one disposition', but the mapping assigns 'native + extension' to one row and 'requires/extension' to others. It does not define whether dispositions apply to whole objects or individual fields.

concerns.recommendation: Define the unit of disposition and represent native/formula output plus extension-preserved fields without assigning conflicting statuses; test field-level coverage in the census.
concerns.title: The disposition rule cannot represent the proposed mixed mappings

evidence.observation: Predicate 9 requires that an upstream contribution 'has been opened', but OS6 says 'It does not block the close: if the PR is still open at close, its state is recorded as a carryover.' The phase graph also places OS6 before close.

concerns.recommendation: State whether an opened PR is mandatory for close, and distinguish an open PR from a PR that has not been posted because its separate owner gate has not been granted.
concerns.title: OS6 has conflicting milestone close criteria

response.summary: The plan needs a consistent loss-report contract, complete treatment of model fields, and a clear OS6 close criterion.

response.summary: Found blocking concerns regarding proprietary dependencies in ordinary gates, unsupported claims about OssieParser, missing element dispositions, stale r1 wording, and phase dependency contradictions.

evidence.location: §2.1 mapping table, line 208; predicate 3, lines 40-44; rule 4, line 87
evidence.observation: The mapping row reads '`reference_populations`, sample populations | none in the ontology; mappings are layer 1 | out of scope', but predicate 3 defines exactly four dispositions — 'native (a core Ossie construct), requires (an Ossie formula), extension (the gnd vendor extension) or refused (a closed reason code)' — and rule 4 states 'One disposition walk over every metaschema element kind decides native/requires/extension/refused. There are no per-kind copies.' 'out of scope' is not a disposition value the published loss-report schema can carry, so a population-bearing census model either breaks the walk (exit 70) or its loss is invisible, violating R8 'Lossless or loud'.

concerns.recommendation: Give populations a real disposition (extension, or refused with a named code) and cover them in the census test, or state explicitly that the OS0-fixed export census excludes population-bearing models and get owner sign-off for that narrowing of predicate 1 ('every packaged example model').
concerns.title: Sample/reference populations have no valid disposition, so their loss cannot be recorded

evidence.location: Predicate 4, lines 45-49; §9 OS2 row, lines 299-302; §4 OS2, lines 296-302
evidence.observation: Predicate 4 claims 'A population that violates a constraint shows the same verdict under GND's checker and under the formula's meaning', but the only Ossie-side instruments named are syntactic: OS2 says each formula is 'checked by OssieParser in the oracle lane, and by GND's own grammar check for the subset it emits in ordinary gates', and §1.1/§7 exclude layers 2–3 (the query engines) from scope. Nothing in the plan evaluates the semantics of an Ossie requires formula independently of GND's own code, so the OS2-C2 differential cases risk comparing GND's checker against GND's own reading of the formula — circular, not differential.

concerns.recommendation: Name in the OS2 spec the independent evaluator of formula semantics for the differential cases (e.g. a small hand-verified expected-verdict table per kind, or an existing upstream semantics tool if one exists at the pinned commit), so OS2-C2 can fail for semantic mismatch, not just parse success.
concerns.title: No independent oracle evaluates requires-formula semantics for the differential claim

evidence.location: Predicate 5, lines 52-53; OD6 ruling, line 448; §2.1 objectification row, line 205
evidence.observation: Predicate 5 requires that 'for a GND-exported document, import restores a model that gnd diff reports as equal to the source (round trip, OS3-C3)', while OD6 (o) rules default export is 'Exit 0 with the loss report' even when elements are refused, and §2.1 marks objectification as 'extension, or refused (OS0 measures)'. A refused element is by definition not in the document, so import cannot restore it and the unqualified round-trip equality cannot hold for any census model that produces a refused disposition.

concerns.recommendation: Scope OS3-C3 explicitly: either restrict round-trip equality to documents whose loss report contains no refused rows (with those models listed in the OS3 spec) or require refused elements to be reconstructible from a recorded reason code; state which in the OS3 spec so the predicate is falsifiable as written.
concerns.title: Round-trip predicate is unqualified for exports that contain refused elements

evidence.location: Header, line 3; §1.4 sources table, line 174; §10 OD8 row, line 450
evidence.observation: The header states 'The owner ruled OD0–OD7 on 2026-11-10', but §1.4 cites 'rulings OD0–OD8 (§10)' and §10 contains an OD8 row with an (o) ruling ('yes' to also trying relationalai 2.0). The header's range is stale by one decision.

concerns.recommendation: Update the header to 'OD0–OD8' so the status line matches §10 and §1.4; no behavioural change.
concerns.title: Header ruling range says OD0–OD7 but §10/§1.4 include OD8

response.summary: Plan is well-structured: predicates are falsifiable and map to phase criteria and named tests/lanes; §10 rulings are consistently applied with r1 wording explicitly tagged; ordinary gates are credential-free under R9; phase order OS0→OS1→{OS2,OS3}→OS4→{OS5,OS6} has no cycle, and the only outward-facing action (OS6 upstream PR) carries a separate owner gate. Four concerns, none blocking: sample/reference populations get the disposition 'out of scope', which is outside predicate 3's closed disposition vocabulary and contradicts rule 4's one-walk-over-every-element-kind; predicate 4's 'same verdict under the formula's meaning' names no independent semantics evaluator, so the differential could be self-referential; the predicate 5 round-trip claim is unqualified even though OD6 permits exit-0 exports containing refused elements that import cannot restore; and the header says the owner ruled OD0–OD7 while §1.4/§10 include OD8.

evidence.observation: Predicate 4 claims: 'A population that violates a constraint shows the same verdict under GND's checker and under the formula's meaning. This is shown by differential cases, one per exported constraint kind (OS2-C2).' The plan names no engine that evaluates an exported formula's meaning over a population: its only Ossie-side instruments are syntactic (section 1.1 lists only validation/validate.py with schemas; OS2 says formulas are 'checked by OssieParser in the oracle lane, and by GND's own grammar check for the subset it emits in ordinary gates'), and section 1.3 records that the sole semantic consumer drops constraints ('the converter emits no require. The Ossie requires constraints of flights.ontology.yaml do not reach PyRel'). As written, the verdict-equivalence half of predicate 4 is not demonstrable with any instrument the plan names.

concerns.recommendation: The OS2 spec must name the second verdict engine for the differential cases -- a GND-side evaluator over the exported formula AST, or pre-recorded golden verdicts per constraint kind -- and record its circularity limits; otherwise weaken predicate 4 to grammar acceptance plus GND-checker verdicts.
concerns.title: Predicate 4's verdict-equivalence claim has no named engine that evaluates the Ossie formula's meaning

evidence.observation: The row reads: '| `reference_populations`, sample populations | none in the ontology; mappings are layer 1 | out of scope |'. 'out of scope' is none of the four dispositions predicate 3 admits ('native ... requires ... extension ... or refused (a closed reason code)'), rule 4 requires 'One disposition walk over every metaschema element kind', and R8 states 'Nothing is dropped silently'. reference_populations is a key of the GND metaschema (src/gnd/schema/orm-meta.schema.json lines 76 and 198), so census models can carry it and the export would emit neither an extension payload nor a refused reason code for it, hollowing out the OS1-C4 census test for those elements. The same section also uses split dispositions ('native + extension') that predicate 3's 'exactly one disposition' does not define.

concerns.recommendation: Assign populations a real disposition in section 2.1 and the loss-report schema -- extension, or refused with a closed reason code such as populations:out-of-scope -- and state how split rows record exactly one disposition, so every metaschema element kind the walk touches has exactly one disposition the census test can fail on.
concerns.title: reference_populations get disposition 'out of scope', outside the four-disposition loss contract the plan claims

evidence.observation: The ruling cell reads: '(o) "why not": read as accepting the proposal. Exit 0 with the loss report; `--strict` turns any `refused` disposition into exit 3. If the owner meant the other reading, this row is re-ruled before OS1's spec'. The one-word reply is genuinely ambiguous, the section 2.3 CLI contract and OS1 tests will encode one reading of it, and the re-rule fires only if the owner volunteers the other reading -- no confirmation step is scheduled anywhere in section 4 or section 8.

concerns.recommendation: Make an explicit OD6 confirmation a listed precondition of the OS1 spec gate (as OS0-C3 does for measurement-dependent rulings), so the default exit-on-loss semantics are not built on an unconfirmed reading.
concerns.title: OD6 default exit semantics rest on an ambiguous one-word ruling with no scheduled confirmation

evidence.observation: '0.1.1 (2025-12-11) is the only release, and it has no ontology.' Section 1.4's source table names only the two pinned git checkouts plus GND and planning files; release history is not derivable from a pinned commit checkout, and the plan's own R7 binds it to 'Never claim more than the pinned bytes.'

concerns.recommendation: Name the source for the release-history claim (upstream tags, CHANGELOG, or a dated PyPI check) in section 1.4, or mark the sentence unverified context.
concerns.title: Unsourced claim that 0.1.1 is Ossie's only release

evidence.observation: 'The owner ruled OD0-OD7 on 2026-11-10' -- but section 10 carries a ruled OD8 row ('(o) "you can also try relationalai 2.0": E3 runs on 1.39.0 and on 2.0.1 (E3b)'), and section 1.4 says 'goal; rulings OD0-OD8 (section 10)', so the r1-era header understates the ruling set the plan actually applies.

concerns.recommendation: Update the status header to OD0-OD8.
concerns.title: Stale r1 header says OD0-OD7 while the plan records rulings OD0-OD8

evidence.observation: 'Contested mapping questions (role order, OneToOne, modality) are settled by experiments on the fixtures.' Of the three named questions only role order has an experiment (E4); the OS0 experiment list E1-E5 and E3b contains none for OneToOne or modality, whose section 2.1 dispositions are therefore fixed without the measurement rule 6 promises.

concerns.recommendation: Either add OS0 experiments or explicit census-inventory checks for OneToOne and modality, or drop them from rule 6's contested list so the measurement claim matches the experiment list.
concerns.title: Rule 6 names OneToOne and modality as experiment-settled, but no OS0 experiment covers them

response.summary: Digest verified. r2 is pinned, measured and owner-ruled: every completion predicate maps to named criteria, tests or lanes; phase order is acyclic with no optional work supplying mandatory prerequisites; ordinary gates stay credential-free with upstream and proprietary tools confined to the opt-in oracle lane; the upstream PR and panel runs carry separate owner gates. Two blocking demonstrability gaps remain in the completion predicates themselves, plus smaller claim-support and internal-consistency defects.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.
Cite one concrete artifact location (section and quoted text) for every concern.
Check that every completion predicate is falsifiable and maps to a phase criterion and a test or lane that can fail it.

Check claims about Apache Ossie (ontology layer 0.3.0.dev0, validator, ossie-converters RelationalAI converter) against what the plan says it read at the pinned commits; flag any claim the plan cannot support.
Check the GND-to-Ossie element mapping (section 2.1) for constructs that would be silently lost or mis-stated, and whether the disposition walk and loss report make every loss visible.
Check that the owner rulings in section 10 are applied consistently everywhere in the plan, with no stale r1 wording contradicting them.
Check that ordinary gates stay credential-free and that proprietary or upstream tools stay out of GND runtime dependencies.
Check phase ordering and dependencies for cycles, missing prerequisites, and optional work supplying mandatory prerequisites.
Reject unbounded execution or outward-facing actions (publication, upstream PRs) that lack a separate owner gate.
